title: Account registration and device enrollment data can be linked to a specific household profile
description: During account registration and camera/sensor enrollment, the Home Hub may combine identity details, account identifiers, device serial numbers, and network metadata into a single profile. This can allow linking multiple devices and activities to the same homeowner or household.
assumptions: The Home Hub stores or forwards registration identifiers together with device identifiers.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort node id; exact LINDDUN Pro subtree for linkability may vary.

title: Registration and enrollment reveal homeowner identity and household composition
description: The registration flow may disclose personally identifying information such as name, email, address, and information about enrolled cameras/sensors. Device types and counts can reveal occupancy patterns, security posture, or household characteristics.
assumptions: The flow contains personal details and device metadata beyond a bare pseudonymous identifier.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort node id; exact LINDDUN Pro subtree for identifiability may vary.

title: Sensitive personal and device details may be disclosed during registration or enrollment
description: If registration credentials, device identifiers, setup secrets, or household details are transmitted or stored insecurely, unauthorized parties could access them. This may expose account data and information about the home security deployment.
assumptions: The flow includes credentials, device IDs, or setup tokens and may traverse networks or logs accessible to other parties.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort node id; exact LINDDUN Pro disclosure subtree may vary.

title: Enrolled devices and account remain detectable as belonging to this household
description: Persistent identifiers such as account IDs, device serial numbers, MAC addresses, or hub enrollment records can make the homeowner's devices detectable over time. Observers or connected services may infer the continued presence of specific sensors or cameras in the home.
assumptions: Enrollment uses stable identifiers that are retained or observable after setup.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort node id; exact LINDDUN Pro detectability subtree may vary.

title: Homeowner may lack awareness of how registration and enrollment data will be used
description: The flow may not clearly inform the homeowner about what personal data, device metadata, and telemetry are collected during account creation and enrollment, how long they are retained, or whether they are shared with vendors or cloud services.
assumptions: Notice and choice mechanisms are limited or not presented at the point of collection.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort node id; exact LINDDUN Pro unawareness subtree may vary.

title: Registration and enrollment may collect more personal data than necessary or process it incompatibly
description: The Home Hub may require excessive personal information or collect unnecessary device metadata during onboarding, beyond what is needed to create an account and enroll cameras/sensors. This can violate data minimization, purpose limitation, or retention expectations.
assumptions: The onboarding design is capable of collecting optional or excessive fields and retaining them longer than needed.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort node id; exact LINDDUN Pro non-compliance subtree may vary.

title: Homeowner may be unable to prove or dispute consent and enrollment actions
description: If the system does not provide reliable records of notices shown, consents given, and devices enrolled, the homeowner may later be unable to repudiate unauthorized enrollment actions or demonstrate that specific privacy choices were made at registration time.
assumptions: The system lacks tamper-evident records or user-visible confirmation of onboarding actions.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort node id; exact LINDDUN Pro non-repudiation/privacy subtree may vary because LINDDUN treatment of repudiation-related privacy issues can be model-specific.

title: Exposure of temporary access code during entry
description: When the guest enters the temporary access code at the Home Hub, the code may be observed by nearby people, captured by cameras, or inferred from input feedback, revealing authentication data associated with the guest visit.
assumptions: The hub is located in a place where others may observe the input process or where visual/audible feedback is available.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id based on interception/disclosure of data in transit from user to system; exact LINDDUN Pro subtree may differ.

title: Home Hub can identify which guest used a specific temporary code
description: If temporary access codes are unique per guest or per visit, the Home Hub can associate code entry events with a specific guest identity or invitation record, reducing anonymity of the guest.
assumptions: Temporary codes are individually assigned, or can be mapped by the hub/backend to a particular guest or household event.
uncertainty_note: Node id is a best-fit for identifiability arising from unique credentials rather than direct identity input.

title: Repeated use of the same temporary code enables linking of guest visits
description: If the same temporary access code is reused across multiple visits or across systems/logs, events can be linked together to build a profile of the guest's visit times and frequency.
assumptions: The code is reused for the same guest, remains valid for multiple entries, or is stored in logs that allow correlation over time.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for linkability through repeated credential use; exact subtree may vary.

title: Guest may be unable to deny having attempted or performed entry
description: Code entry and door unlock events may be logged by the Home Hub with timestamps, allowing the household to use those records as evidence that a specific guest accessed or attempted to access the door.
assumptions: The hub logs code submissions or successful unlocks and temporary codes are attributable to individual guests.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for detectability of actions leading to non-repudiation; exact LINDDUN Pro node may differ.

title: Guest may not be adequately informed how temporary code data is processed
description: The guest may enter a temporary code without being informed whether the code entry is logged, how long logs are retained, whether failed attempts are stored, or whether data is shared with other services or household members.
assumptions: No clear notice or consent mechanism is presented to the guest at the hub or beforehand.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for lack of transparency/consent around collection and processing; exact subtree may differ.

title: Code entry behavior may reveal presence or intent to enter the home
description: Even if the guest is not directly identified, observing or logging that a temporary code was entered at a specific time reveals that someone associated with the household is present or attempting entry, exposing private activity patterns.
assumptions: Entry attempts or unlock events are observable through device indicators, logs, notifications, or side channels.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for detectability of an interaction/event; exact LINDDUN Pro subtree may differ.

title: Sensitive occupancy patterns disclosed through local event log contents
description: The local event log stores motion, door, and sensor events that can reveal when residents are home, asleep, away, or moving within the house. Anyone with access to the datastore or its outputs could infer intimate household behavior from the recorded events.
assumptions: Assumes the local event log can be accessed by local administrators, maintenance staff, malware, or other components beyond the minimum need-to-know.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for disclosure of stored personal data; exact LINDDUN Pro subnode may vary by catalog version.

title: Residents can be identified from persistent event histories
description: Even if log entries do not directly name individuals, a persistent history of motion/door/sensor events tied to one home can identify specific residents or households through routine patterns, occupancy schedules, and contextual knowledge.
assumptions: Assumes event logs are associated with a specific household, account, device, or address.
uncertainty_note: Node id is a best-fit estimate for identifiability from stored data; exact subnode may differ in LINDDUN Pro.

title: Event records enable linking of actions over time
description: The log aggregates multiple sensor events over time, allowing separate actions and observations to be linked into a continuous profile of household routines and behaviors.
assumptions: Assumes entries share timestamps, device identifiers, household identifiers, or other stable correlators.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for linkability via correlated records; exact node numbering may vary.

title: Inference of special situations from event combinations
description: Combinations of motion, door, and sensor events may disclose sensitive situations such as vacations, sleep schedules, religious practices, disabilities, caregiving routines, or security incidents, beyond the original operational purpose of logging.
assumptions: Assumes analysis of event sequences or combinations is possible by an attacker or secondary user.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit estimate for indirect disclosure/inference from logged data; exact node id may differ.

title: Logging may occur without resident awareness or expectation
description: Residents and visitors may be unaware that fine-grained motion, door, and sensor events are being persistently written to a local log, making the processing insufficiently detectable or transparent to data subjects.
assumptions: Assumes no clear notice, UI indicator, or documentation is provided at the point of collection/logging.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for unawareness about ongoing collection/storage; exact LINDDUN Pro numbering may vary.

title: Retention of detailed event logs may exceed privacy expectations or obligations
description: Persistently storing detailed household event data in the local log may violate data minimization, purpose limitation, retention, or transparency requirements if more data is kept than necessary or for too long.
assumptions: Assumes no explicit retention limit, minimization policy, or lawful basis/consent management is enforced for these logs.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for non-compliance related to excessive retention/minimization; exact subnode may vary by LINDDUN Pro version.

title: Event log could be used as privacy-invasive evidence about occupants' actions
description: Recorded sensor events may later be used to assert that a resident opened a door, moved at a certain time, or was present/absent, creating privacy risk if individuals cannot reasonably contest the interpretation or provenance of the logs.
assumptions: Assumes logs are treated as authoritative evidence in disputes, monitoring, or enforcement contexts.
uncertainty_note: Applicability depends on whether the system relies on the log for accountability or adjudication; node id is a best-fit estimate.

title: Exposure of sensitive video content during upload
description: Recorded camera clips contain highly sensitive personal data about occupants, visitors, routines, and possibly private spaces. If the upload channel or endpoint handling is inadequately protected, unauthorized parties could access the clip contents while they are being transferred from the Home Hub to cloud storage.
assumptions: Assumes clips are transmitted over a network path that could be observed or intercepted, or that endpoint protections are insufficient.
uncertainty_note: Tree node id is my best fit for disclosure of data in transit, but exact LINDDUN Pro subnode naming may vary.

title: Unauthorized disclosure of stored camera clips in cloud storage
description: Once uploaded, cloud video storage may expose clips to unauthorized internal staff, compromised accounts, other tenants, or attackers if access controls, segregation, or encryption at rest are insufficient. This could reveal intimate household activities and behavior patterns.
assumptions: Assumes cloud storage retains uploaded clips and that storage-side access control or key management weaknesses are plausible.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort node id for disclosure from stored data; exact subnode label may differ in LINDDUN Pro.

title: Linkability of clips across time and household activity
description: Cloud-stored clips can be linked over time to build a longitudinal profile of a household, including occupancy schedules, recurring visitors, habits, and events. Even if individual clips seem isolated, shared identifiers, account metadata, timestamps, and camera identifiers can enable strong linkage.
assumptions: Assumes stored clips are associated with persistent account, device, or timestamp metadata.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort node id for linkability via persistent identifiers/metadata; exact node may differ.

title: Identification of occupants or visitors from uploaded video
description: Video clips may directly reveal faces, voices, body characteristics, home interior details, address indicators, or other identifying attributes. Cloud storage and associated metadata can therefore enable identification of specific individuals captured by the cameras.
assumptions: Assumes clips contain human subjects or contextual identifiers such as recognizable surroundings.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort node id for direct identification from content; exact LINDDUN Pro node may vary.

title: Lack of transparency about cloud retention and secondary use of clips
description: Individuals recorded by the cameras, and possibly even the device owner, may not be adequately informed about how long clips are retained in cloud storage, who can access them, whether they are used for analytics or model training, or under what conditions they are shared onward.
assumptions: Assumes the system does not clearly communicate storage practices, downstream access, or secondary uses.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort node for unawareness due to insufficient notice/transparency; exact subnode may differ.

title: Inability to exercise deletion or control over uploaded clips
description: If users cannot easily review, delete, or manage uploaded recordings in cloud storage, they may lose practical control over highly sensitive footage. This is especially problematic for clips containing bystanders or outdated recordings that should no longer be retained.
assumptions: Assumes cloud storage may retain clips beyond user expectations or provide limited management controls.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort node for user loss of control over personal data; exact LINDDUN Pro node may differ.

title: Excessive retention or incompatible processing of uploaded video
description: Cloud storage may keep camera clips longer than necessary, process them for analytics beyond the original home-security purpose, or share them in ways incompatible with the initial collection context. Such practices may violate data minimization, purpose limitation, or storage limitation expectations.
assumptions: Assumes the service could retain or repurpose clips beyond what is necessary for the stated function.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort node for non-compliance with retention/purpose limitation; exact node naming may vary.

title: Insufficient evidence of upload consent or accountability for recorded subjects
description: The Home Hub may upload clips containing occupants, visitors, or bystanders without any reliable record of notice, consent where required, or justification for transfer. This can make it difficult to demonstrate compliant handling of recorded individuals' data and to resolve disputes about whether uploads were authorized.
assumptions: Assumes the environment may include non-owners or bystanders and that accountability records are limited.
uncertainty_note: Node id is a best-effort fit for non-repudiation/accountability gaps rather than classic security repudiation; exact LINDDUN Pro mapping may differ.

title: Linkability of motion alerts to a specific household or device
description: Repeated real-time motion alerts sent from the Home Hub to the mobile app backend may carry persistent device, household, or account identifiers. The backend can link multiple alerts over time to the same home, enabling profiling of occupancy patterns and routines.
assumptions: The flow contains stable identifiers, network metadata, or account binding that let the backend correlate alerts over time.
uncertainty_note: Node id is a best-effort LINDDUN Pro mapping for linkability at the data-flow level; exact subnode may vary by threat tree version.

title: Identifiability of residents from motion alert content or metadata
description: Motion alerts and accompanying metadata such as device ID, account ID, home location, timestamps, or IP-derived context can allow the backend to identify the household or infer the identity of residents associated with the alert.
assumptions: The backend has access to subscriber records or other data sources that map alert metadata to a natural person or household.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort node selection for identifiability; exact node numbering may differ across LINDDUN Pro editions.

title: Detectability of in-home activity from observable alert traffic
description: The existence, timing, frequency, and size of motion-alert messages make in-home movement detectable to the backend and potentially to observers with access to transmission metadata. Even without full payload inspection, traffic patterns can reveal when motion occurred.
assumptions: Traffic metadata or message headers are visible to the backend and possibly intermediaries.
uncertainty_note: Tree node is an approximate detectability mapping for inferring event occurrence from message presence and metadata.

title: Disclosure of occupancy patterns and behavioral routines
description: A stream of real-time motion alerts exposes sensitive information about when people are home, asleep, active, away, or following regular routines. This data can reveal intimate behavior patterns beyond the immediate security purpose.
assumptions: Alert timestamps are stored, analyzed, or accessible at the backend beyond transient delivery.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort node id for disclosure of sensitive personal information inferred from the data flow.

title: Unawareness of backend use and retention of motion-alert data
description: Residents may be unaware that the backend receives, stores, analyzes, or repurposes real-time motion alerts, including deriving occupancy analytics or sharing data for operations, security, or product improvement.
assumptions: Not all affected residents are directly informed through the app or notices, and retention/secondary uses may not be obvious.
uncertainty_note: Node id is approximate for lack of transparency/awareness regarding collection and processing.

title: Processing motion-alert data beyond stated purpose or legal basis
description: If the backend uses motion alerts for analytics, profiling, model training, marketing, or prolonged retention beyond delivering the alert, the processing may violate purpose limitation, data minimization, or retention obligations.
assumptions: Applicable privacy requirements constrain secondary use, minimization, transparency, or retention for home activity data.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort non-compliance node selection; exact LINDDUN Pro subnode depends on the compliance obligation in scope.

title: Insufficient evidence about consent or user choices for sending alerts
description: The Home Hub may forward motion alerts without reliable evidence that the account holder configured, enabled, or consented to this transmission, making it hard to demonstrate what privacy choices were in effect when data was sent.
assumptions: User configuration and consent state are relevant to whether this flow should occur and may not be securely bound to each transmitted alert.
uncertainty_note: Repudiation-related privacy threats are less central for this flow; applicability and exact node id are somewhat uncertain.

title: Exposure of occupancy information through notification content
description: A motion-detected push notification can disclose personal information about activity at the home, such as presence, absence, or movement patterns, if the notification content is visible on the device lock screen, intercepted in transit, or observed by someone other than the homeowner.
assumptions: Notification text contains event details such as motion detection and may appear on the phone lock screen or notification banner.
uncertainty_note: Tree node id is my best fit for information disclosure of message contents on a data flow; exact LINDDUN Pro node naming may vary.

title: Linkability of repeated motion events to a specific household
description: Repeated notifications from the backend to the same homeowner device can be linked over time, allowing an observer or intermediary to correlate motion events and infer household routines or occupancy patterns for a particular home/account.
assumptions: Push delivery uses stable identifiers such as device tokens, account identifiers, or consistent metadata visible to intermediaries or the platform.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort node selection for linkability via repeated messages on a flow; exact node id may differ in LINDDUN Pro.

title: Identifiability of the homeowner from notification metadata
description: Notification routing metadata or payload fields may directly or indirectly identify the homeowner, household, account, device, or address, enabling the recipient or an intermediary to associate the motion event with a specific person or residence.
assumptions: The push mechanism or payload includes identifiers, account references, location labels, or device-specific tokens.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort node selection for identifiability from data-flow metadata; exact node id may vary.

title: Unawareness of notification recipients or visibility scope
description: The homeowner may be unaware that motion notifications can appear on lock screens, be mirrored to wearables, shared devices, or notification previews, causing broader exposure of home activity data than expected.
assumptions: Default device or app settings allow notification previews or cross-device notification syncing.
uncertainty_note: Node id is a best estimate for lack of transparency/awareness about privacy-relevant processing and exposure.

title: Notifications may be sent without valid or current user consent/preferences
description: The backend may continue sending motion-detected notifications despite outdated consent, revoked preferences, or insufficiently granular privacy settings, resulting in processing and disclosure of home-activity data beyond what the homeowner agreed to.
assumptions: Notification preferences or consent states may be stale, unsynchronized, or not sufficiently specific for event types.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort node selection for non-compliance around consent/preference enforcement on this flow.

title: Analytics payload may remain linkable to individual users or devices
description: Although described as aggregated device-usage analytics, the backend may share stable identifiers, coarse aggregation buckets, rare events, timestamps, or segment combinations that allow the cloud analytics vendor to link records to the same device, account, or household over time.
assumptions: Assumes the aggregation is not fully anonymizing and that the vendor receives repeated submissions or metadata enabling correlation.
uncertainty_note: Tree node id is my best estimate for linkability from a data flow; exact LINDDUN Pro node naming may vary.

title: Vendor can infer sensitive traits from aggregated usage analytics
description: Even if direct identifiers are removed, aggregated usage patterns can reveal or support inference about user behavior, preferences, routines, location patterns, health-related app usage, or membership in small cohorts when combined with the vendor's other datasets.
assumptions: Assumes the vendor has analytical capability and possibly auxiliary datasets to enrich the received analytics.
uncertainty_note: Node id is an approximate best fit for inferability in LINDDUN Pro.

title: Vendor may detect participation of a specific user or small group in the dataset
description: If the shared analytics contains small-cell aggregates, unusual event counts, or narrowly defined segments, the vendor may be able to determine that a specific person, device, or tiny cohort is represented in the analytics submission.
assumptions: Assumes some aggregates are computed over small populations or highly specific segments.
uncertainty_note: Exact detectability subtree node may differ; this is my best estimate.

title: Re-identification through combination with external data
description: The cloud analytics vendor may combine the received aggregated analytics with other customer data, ad-tech identifiers, telemetry, or public datasets to single out users or devices, effectively disclosing identities behind ostensibly aggregated statistics.
assumptions: Assumes the vendor has access to auxiliary datasets and the aggregation granularity is sufficiently fine to support singling out.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort node id for disclosure of information via re-identification; exact LINDDUN Pro node may vary.

title: Analytics sharing may exceed user consent or stated purpose
description: Sharing analytics with an external cloud analytics vendor may be incompatible with the purpose originally communicated to users, or may occur without valid consent, opt-out honoring, or an appropriate legal basis for third-party analytics processing.
assumptions: Assumes analytics sharing is subject to privacy notice, consent, or other legal-basis requirements.
uncertainty_note: Node id is an approximate best fit for non-compliance / unlawful processing.

title: Users may be unaware of third-party analytics disclosure
description: Users may not realize that their app usage contributes to analytics sent to an external vendor, especially if disclosures are buried in privacy notices or aggregation is presented as harmless without explaining downstream third-party processing.
assumptions: Assumes limited transparency in the app's notices or consent UI.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort node id for unawareness; exact subtree mapping may differ.

title: Video clip content exposed to unauthorized backend-side access
description: When the mobile app backend retrieves a stored video clip from cloud storage, insufficient authorization on the storage read path could allow backend components, service accounts, or misrouted requests to access clips belonging to a different homeowner, exposing intimate in-home footage.
assumptions: Cloud video clips contain personal data and are expected to be accessible only for the entitled homeowner/session context.
uncertainty_note: Node id is my best fit for information disclosure via unauthorized read/access on this flow; exact LINDDUN Pro subtree naming may vary.

title: Backend returns the wrong stored clip to the requester
description: If object references, account binding, or tenancy checks are flawed, the backend may retrieve and serve a video clip associated with another user, disclosing personal household activity to an unauthorized recipient.
assumptions: The backend is responsible for enforcing ownership and tenant isolation before or during retrieval from storage.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for disclosure caused by missing/incorrect authorization or object binding; exact node naming may differ.

title: Retrieval requests enable linkage of multiple clips to the same household or user
description: Stable storage object identifiers, account-scoped paths, or repeated retrieval patterns may allow the backend or observers with access to logs/metadata to link multiple video clips to the same homeowner over time, building a profile of activity.
assumptions: Metadata such as clip IDs, storage paths, or account identifiers are persistent across accesses and visible to components handling the flow.
uncertainty_note: Tree node is a best estimate for linkability via persistent identifiers/metadata on the flow.

title: Video retrieval metadata reveals homeowner behavior patterns
description: Even if clip contents are protected, the act of requesting playback can disclose that someone is reviewing footage at a certain time, and clip identifiers/timestamps can reveal when motion events occurred, exposing occupancy, routines, or incidents.
assumptions: Access logs, timestamps, or request metadata are available to backend operators, analytics systems, or other internal recipients.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for detectability through observable metadata/logging; exact LINDDUN Pro node may differ.

title: Presence of a stored clip makes household events detectable
description: The existence, size, naming, or timestamp of a stored video object can make it detectable that a camera recorded an event at a particular time, even before content is viewed, revealing patterns such as arrivals, departures, or alarms.
assumptions: Storage metadata is visible to backend services or administrators beyond strict need-to-know.
uncertainty_note: Node id is an approximate mapping for detectability based on storage object existence/metadata.

title: Playback retrieval uses video for purposes beyond the homeowner playback purpose
description: The backend retrieval path may also feed analytics, model training, employee troubleshooting, or service improvement workflows without a compatible legal basis or without honoring the original purpose limitation for storing the clip.
assumptions: The same retrieval or copied data may be reused internally beyond immediate playback delivery.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit non-compliance node for purpose limitation/legal basis issues; exact node id may vary across LINDDUN Pro versions.

title: Homeowner may be unaware that clip retrieval generates additional processing and logs
description: Users may believe playback simply streams their clip, while the backend may create access logs, cached copies, thumbnails, or analytics events that are not transparent to them, undermining predictability and awareness of processing.
assumptions: The service performs secondary processing during retrieval that is not clearly explained in notices or UI.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for lack of awareness/transparency; exact U subtree node may differ.
